label: <DEL> step of long sequences with an early k (sparse)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.3% of delimiter steps). 85% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (t = L), mostly in long sequences (L = 8-9 hold ~88% of mass). Within those, it prefers sequences with k as the 2nd or 3rd original token (kk is common in the top examples), first tokens h/r/y/0/b/m/z, and last original token c or w. Weaker activations also show up on the last 1-3 original tokens just before <DEL>. It almost never fires in the copy phase or on the first three tokens. The predicate (delimiter, L>=8, k at position 1 or 2) gets about half the mass but only ~6.5% precision on dev. Which delimiter steps fire looks like a soft conjunction of many token-identity factors that no simple predicate captures. Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.26), and the top activations are in L>=8 sequences that start with kk.
